BLOCK - round 1, PR #292, head d398803f7169ef29f136704536205e8c8210ae06, comparison base 27076a37.

R292-001 HIGH, confidence 10/10: the alone branch kills a remaining real-work pane.
Location: crates/tmux/src/control.rs:89-93; Live::leave at 231-250.
The predicate proves one client, one window and one pane, not that this is the idle control pane. Reproduced with the exact production TmuxAdapter on tmux 3.6a: start main, attach the control client, create a real-work window in _pij, and close the original idle window. Immediately before exit, list-clients reports 1:_pij, list-windows reports real-work:1, and destroy-unattached is off. Both drop(adapter) and adapter.release_control() then delete _pij and the real-work pane; main survives. This is introduced data loss: the prior Drop only killed the client and respected the hook's destroy-unattached off.
Required correction: make teardown distinguish actual idle control work from a sole remaining real-work pane. Keep both drop and release regressions; each must preserve the real pane after closing the original control window.

R292-002 MEDIUM, confidence 10/10: the advertised one-second exit bound does not include the write.
Location: crates/tmux/src/control.rs:245-250; crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:398-399.
Mechanically extracted the exact Live fields, Drop, leave, TEARDOWN constants and command_line implementation without modifying the review worktree. An owned, nonreading child with a full 65,536-byte stdin pipe held Drop beyond a five-second watchdog. Only the watchdog's targeted kill unblocked it; elapsed was 5,013 ms. Removing only the new self.leave() call returned in 0 ms. recv_timeout begins after blocking write_all/flush, so it never starts in this case; the daemon also awaits the blocking release without a bound. The existing cat fixture continuously drains stdin and proves only the reply wait.
Required correction: bound the whole teardown, including a backpressured write, and retain an external owned-pid deadline fixture. A timeout around awaiting spawn_blocking alone does not stop its blocking work.

Requested checks:
- The fixed if-shell format is not built from untrusted input. It executes over the still-attached pipe. Its count predicate is insufficient for real-work preservation (R292-001).
- Ordinary adapter drop, failed/slow reply replacement, Alone and explicit release reach Live::drop. release marks the state permanently released; the existing release regression passes.
- Closed-reader and unanswered-reply regressions pass, but do not establish the full write bound (R292-002).
- Isolated offline daemons from an exact-head CLI snapshot handled both SIGINT and SIGTERM: exit 0, graceful-shutdown banner present, 4 ms each. The handler chooses one signal then consumes Daemon in one shutdown; the existing worker/HTTP join and delivery/event flush remain in place. This signal probe is not live-fleet or in-flight-delivery proof.
- just bounce-rs: after 150 nominal 0.2-second sleeps it sends SIGKILL to the old pid, ignores kill failures, and launches immediately without establishing post-KILL exit. This is an iteration budget, not a strict elapsed 30-second deadline. A new daemon cannot take an occupied port: boot binds before building services or mutating shared state. If the old daemon already dropped its listener while draining, the port alone does not prove that its control client has exited. Performance owns these timeout/launch findings in BLOCK 6f069620dfa17233b28b1a567e6b081776510290.
- Old state-root and new socket-root locks are different files; there is no mixed-version serialization bridge. A healthy serial bounce waits for the old pid to disappear before starting the new daemon, which avoids the overlap. Coexisting old/new daemons, or the unconfirmed forced-exit path, are not protected by one common lock.
- Destructive behavior is not merely reordered: R292-001 changes a previously kept real-work session into deletion. The count guard is a brake around killing, but counts are not pane identity. The attach lock is a brake: it can only delay/refuse attach.
